title: Winter Returns to Palestine as People in Gaza Brace for the Cold Without Adequate Shelter
excerpt: Winter is approaching once again in Palestine. With shelter and supplies in short supply, winter aid is a vital need for vulnerable families.
seoTitle: Winter Returns to Palestine as Gaza Braces - Relawan Nusantara
seoDescription: Winter is approaching once again in Palestine. With shelter and supplies in short supply, winter aid is a vital need for vulnerable families.
html:
For some people, winter may mean cool air, warm clothes, and time spent together with family at home.

But for many Palestinian families, winter arrives with a different kind of worry.

It is not only about falling temperatures, but about how to get through the night when their shelter does not offer enough protection from the cold, rain, wind, and even floods.

As the 2026–2027 winter sets in, these conditions are once again a humanitarian concern. The latest report from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) on 2 October 2026 states that humanitarian partners in Gaza are stepping up preparations for the winter and rainy season, including repairing drainage, reinforcing shelters, and reducing flood risks at displacement sites. However, these efforts still face constraints in funding, access, and the entry of essential materials and supplies.

For those living in tents or damaged buildings, a change in the weather is not merely an inconvenience. It can become a new threat to safety and health.

When Tents Are Not Enough to Keep Out the Cold

For years, conflict and forced displacement have left many Palestinian families living far from their homes.

In Gaza, inadequate shelter makes winter feel far harsher. Tents and temporary shelters must withstand rain, strong winds, standing water, and low nighttime temperatures.

OCHA notes that this year's winter preparations still face shortages of shelter supplies and non-food needs. The available stock covers around 17,000 tents, tarpaulins, and sealing-off kits for around 50,000 families, winter clothing for around 9,000 families, and bedding for around 50,000 families. However, these quantities are still insufficient compared with the scale of need in Gaza.

The risk does not come from the cold alone, either.

Fragile shelters, poor drainage, and heavy rain can cause water to enter tents or displacement areas. Wet and damp conditions can then worsen health problems, especially for children, the elderly, and people with vulnerable health conditions.

Children Are Among the Most Vulnerable Groups

Winter always brings greater risks for children living in displacement.

In January 2026, UNRWA described how cold, heavy rain, and flooding worsened health risks for children in Gaza. These conditions unfolded amid overcrowded displacement sites and limited water, sanitation, and health services.

OCHA also estimates that around 650,000 children in Gaza need winterization support for child protection. More than 450 child-friendly spaces and safe spaces operate in Gaza, but more than 90 percent of them are in tents or temporary structures that remain vulnerable to rain, flooding, wind, and cold temperatures.

For that reason, winter aid is not only about providing warm clothing.

Blankets, mattresses, bedding, tarpaulins, winter clothing, and safer shelter can all be an important part of helping families get through the winter better protected.

Winter Is Not Only a Matter of Temperature

There is one thing that is often forgotten when talking about winter in conflict areas: the cold arrives when many basic needs have yet to be met.

For families who live in intact homes and have electricity, heating, warm clothes, and enough food, low temperatures may feel like nothing more than a change in the weather.

But for families living in tents or damaged buildings, the cold comes together with other problems.

How do you dry wet clothes?

How do you keep a child warm when there are not enough blankets?

How do you protect your shelter from the rain?

And how do you get a warm meal when fuel and basic necessities are also limited?

For that reason, winter preparation is an important part of the humanitarian response.

OCHA states that these needs are becoming more urgent as winter draws closer, while stocks of shelter supplies and non-food items remain limited.

A Trust to Deliver Winter Aid

These needs are not something that is only talked about from afar.

Relawan Nusantara, together with Konsorsium Kebaikan Indonesia, has on several occasions helped deliver aid to Palestinians facing the winter.

On 7 January 2026, humanitarian aid was distributed to displaced families at Jabal Nadzif Camp. The aid included ready-to-eat meals, staple foods, and winter aid to help families cope with the cold weather.

Earlier, aid was also distributed to refugee camps in the border area of the West Bank. In that distribution, Konsorsium Kebaikan Indonesia, together with partners including Relawan Nusantara, delivered 200 winter aid packages, 200 food packages, and 400 ready-to-eat meal packages to families in need.

This aid may not change the whole of the situation they face.

But one winter aid package can help a family get through the night a little warmer.

One food package can help meet that day's needs.

And one act of care can be a reminder that they are not alone.

From Indonesia, Warmth Continues to Be Sent

Indonesia and Palestine are thousands of kilometers apart.

But humanity does not stop because of distance.

Every piece of aid sent is an expression of care from people who choose to remain present, even when they cannot be there in person among the Palestinian people.

Winter is coming again.

For some people, it may be just a season. But for families living in hardship, winter can be yet another trial to get through.

For that reason, providing blankets, warm clothes, food, bedding, and winter necessities is not merely giving goods.

It is a simple way to bring a sense of warmth to circumstances that are still far from easy.

Relawan Nusantara, together with donors and partners, will keep striving so that care from Indonesia can reach those in need.

Because when the cold comes, may not a single family feel that they have to face it alone. Let us help Palestine through the winter.

Luaskan Manfaat
